chunks: No believer leaves this world except with contentment from Him. That is because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, lifts the veil for him until he looks at his place in Paradise and what Allah has prepared for him therein. And the world is displayed before him in the best way it ever was for him, then he is given the choice, so he chooses what is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and says: What have I to do with the world and its afflictions?
So prompt your dying ones with the Words of Relief.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life that the believer leaves behind
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the believer’s shown destination and reward
key_terms.الْغِطَاءَ: the veil that Allah removes so the unseen reality becomes visible
key_terms.بَلَائِهَا: the afflictions and trials of worldly life
key_terms.كَلِمَاتِ الْفَرَجِ: the Words of Relief to be prompted to the dying
key_terms.مَوْتَاكُمْ: your dying ones or those near death
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٌ: a believer, the one whose departing state is described here

ai.seo_question: Why does a believer leave this world with contentment, and what should be recited to the dying?
ai.summary: The hadith teaches that a believer departs this world with contentment because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, reveals to him his place in Paradise and what has been prepared for him there. Seeing the reality of the Hereafter, he prefers what is with Allah over the world and its afflictions, which is why the dying are to be prompted with the Words of Relief.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.355 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"No believer leaves this world except with contentment, for Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, lifts the veil for them until they see their place in Paradise and what Allah (swt) has prepared for them there. Then the world is shown to them as the best it could have been, and they are given the choice, so they choose what is with Allah (swt), Mighty and Glorious, and say,
'What do I need with the world and its trials?'
Therefore, instruct your dying with the Words of Relief (Kalimat E Faraj)."
Lā ilāha illā Allāh al-Ḥalīmu al-Karīm, lā ilāha illā Allāh al-‘Aliyyu al-‘Aẓīm.
Subḥāna Allāhi Rabbi al-samāwāti al-sab‘ wa Rabbi al-arāḍīna al-sab‘ wa mā fīhinna wa mā baynahunna wa mā taḥtahunna wa Rabbi al-‘arsh al-‘Aẓīm
